name: Deep-learning automated geosteering: GAN earth models plus ensemble data assimilation (DISTINGUISH), MDN/multiple-trajectory-prediction relative-position predictors, CNN/RNN stratigraphic correlators, and GenAI explainable decision support (2020-2026)
authors_org: Main line: Sergey Alyaev, Kristian Fossum, Jan Tveranger, Ahmed H. Elsheikh, Reidar Bratvold, Igor Cheraghi and co-authors, from NORCE, Heriot-Watt and University of Stavanger (DISTINGUISH project, geosteering-no GitHub org). Related correlators: SPE ATCE 2020 'Deep-Learning-Based Automated Stratigraphic Correlation'; Yang et al. 2023 ASDNet (attention dense net); 'Stratigraphic Correlation of Well Logs Using Geology-Informed Deep Learning Networks' (Processes 2025); intra/inter-well constrained stratigraphic-layer identification (2025).

code_availability: DISTINGUISH workflow (GAN + FNN EM proxy + EnKF + DP decision support): https://github.com/geosteering-no/DISTINGUISH-WF, with pre-trained models via git LFS. MDN-MTP multi-modal GR inversion (ESS 2022): code not confirmed [uncertain]. ASDNet / Processes 2025 correlators: no public code found [uncertain].
evidence_level: Peer-reviewed (First Break 2021, ICCS 2021, J. Comput. Sci. 2022, ESS 2022, Processes 2025, ASDNet 2023) plus arXiv preprints (2503.08509 v2, 2210.15548). All GAN/EnKF geosteering results are synthetic. Full-text numbers were verified only for 2503.08509 (HTML); the rest come from abstracts.
extreme_summary: Two DL routes to geosteering. (1) GANs trained offline encode complex 2D geology in a roughly 60-dimensional latent vector, a neural forward proxy simulates EM/resistivity logs, and an ensemble smoother (EnRML/EnKF) updates the latent ensemble in real time, followed by DP/robust optimisation for decisions. (2) Direct inversion networks (MDN trained with a multiple-trajectory-prediction loss) map GR along the well to several probable stratigraphic curves with probabilities in milliseconds, avoiding the mode collapse of standard MDNs.
task_definition: Route 1: estimate the 2D geology around and ahead of the bit (facies/resistivity section), then choose the next steering move. Route 2 (closest to our task): from a GR log measured along the lateral plus a reference stratigraphy, predict the well's stratigraphic position/offset curve (the relative position to the layers) as multiple weighted hypotheses, including ahead of the data. Correlators (ASDNet etc.) label formation tops per depth, mostly in vertical wells.
inputs: Route 1: ultra-deep azimuthal resistivity (UDAR) / extra-deep EM measurements, trajectory, a prior ensemble of 250 latent vectors. Route 2: gamma-ray along the trajectory plus the implicit reference stratigraphy learned from training geology; single-well only. Correlators: multi-log suites (GR, resistivity, density, etc.) across vertical wells; the 2025 work adds intra- and inter-well constraints.
target_parameterisation: Route 1: GAN latent vector z (about 60-dimensional standard Gaussian) generating 64x64 facies/property sections. Route 2: stratigraphic offset/position curve along MD relative to the typewell, a TVT-like curve, discretised in grid cells. Correlators: per-depth formation class labels.
output_representation: Route 1: an ensemble of 250 geomodel realisations (a posterior sample set) plus an optimal next action. Route 2: K hypothesis curves with probabilities (mixture/MTP head), i.e. explicit multi-hypothesis output. Correlators: per-depth class probabilities (segmentation).
architecture: Route 1 (DISTINGUISH): a convolutional GAN generator (offline-trained on outcrop-based fluvial models, Williams Fork analogues) maps z to a 2D section. A forward deep neural network (FDNN/FNN) emulates a commercial extra-deep EM simulator, so the full forward model G(z) to logs is differentiable and fast. An ensemble randomized maximum likelihood (EnRML) or EnKF iteratively updates the 250-member latent ensemble from logs. A dynamic-programming algorithm builds reward matrices per realisation, and a robust step picks the move with maximal mean expected reward. Route 2 (ESS 2022 / SPWLA 2022): a deep network mapping the GR sequence to K candidate stratigraphic curves plus K mixture weights (mixture density network head trained with a multiple-trajectory-prediction loss borrowed from autonomous-driving trajectory forecasting). Correlators: 1D CNN/RNN, attention-based dense nets (ASDNet) and semantic-segmentation networks over log depth.
core_mechanism: Route 1: amortise geological realism into a GAN prior so that data assimilation searches a low-dimensional, geologically plausible manifold, keeping uncertainty as an ensemble. Route 2: a winner-takes-all / MTP loss trains K heads to cover distinct modes, such as distinct repeated-band alignments, and a classification loss learns their probabilities. This avoids the averaging or collapse of a unimodal regressor and gives explicit, scoreable alternative interpretations in milliseconds.
training_objective: GAN: adversarial loss (offline). FDNN: supervised regression to simulator outputs. Data assimilation: EnRML/EnKF misfit minimisation (no network training at run time). MDN-MTP: multiple-trajectory-prediction loss, i.e. regression on the best-matching hypothesis plus cross-entropy on which hypothesis wins. Correlators: cross-entropy per depth; the 2025 geology-informed work adds stratigraphic-order constraints to fix implausible results such as older formations above younger ones or repeated formations at wrong depths.
decoding: Route 1: ensemble statistics and a robust (mean-reward) decision. Route 2: returns all K curves with probabilities; a single answer would be the argmax hypothesis (mode) or the probability-weighted mean. Papers emphasise the multi-modal set rather than one decode.
metric_consistent_decode: Route 2's natural 'most probable curve' decode is mode-seeking (bad for pooled RMSE). The probability-weighted mean of the K curves is RMSE-consistent if the weights are calibrated. Route 1 uses ensemble means for decisions (RMSE-consistent in spirit).
evidence_scope: Whole lateral so far (sequential/real-time), single well plus prior geology. There is no joint multi-well evidence except the 2025 inter-well-constrained correlator.
prefix_conditioning: Route 1: sequential assimilation, where drilled-section data condition the ensemble ahead of the bit. Route 2 (SPWLA 2022 'sequential'): sequential re-inversion as data arrive [uncertain]. No closed-form offset/slope correction from known labels.
propose_vs_select: Route 2 is natively propose-and-select (K hypotheses plus scores), so it can feed a gate/reranker or act as an ensemble member. Route 1 proposes an ensemble and selects by decision optimisation.
physical_constraints: Route 1: geological realism via the GAN prior, physics via the EM forward proxy. Route 2: whatever geology the training generator contains (fixed-thickness stratigraphy with possible faults). Correlators: explicit stratigraphic ordering (2025).
dataset: Route 1: synthetic 2D 64x64 sections cut from a 3D fluvial model based on Williams Fork Formation outcrops, prior ensemble of 250; the Goliat field case study (Barents Sea) for the strategic workflow. Route 2: synthetic layered geologies with GR logs; later NORCE work used the GWC 2020 semifinal GR log. Correlators: field well sets (e.g. Norwegian/Chinese basins), region-specific.
synthetic_to_real: Route 1 and Route 2 are trained entirely on synthetic geology; no sim-to-real alignment is reported. Route 2 uses real GR textures in some variants. None report a real-lateral holdout comparable to ROGII.
metric_and_performance: First Break 2021: GAN+ensemble smoother 'correctly predicts most major geological features up to 500 m ahead of the bit' (qualitative). 2503.08509: qualitative convergence toward the optimal target; UDAR reduces uncertainty more than the older EM tool generation; decisions stay consistent under a biased prior ensemble. ESS 2022 abstract: multi-modal results in milliseconds, mode collapse avoided. A related search snippet reports mean absolute error below 1.5 grid cells on gamma-ray logs with about 1.5 ms evaluation, versus minutes for state-of-the-art inversion [uncertain]; the source is likely ESS 2022 or SPWLA 2022 (see A09). ASDNet: improved formation-label accuracy but with geologically implausible outputs.
comparability: Not comparable. Metrics are in grid cells on synthetic geology, qualitative, or formation-label accuracy in vertical wells; none are pooled TVT RMSE in feet on real laterals.
validation_protocol: Synthetic hold-out realisations and twin experiments (truth sampled from the prior). No spatially grouped real-well CV and no leaderboard.
inference_budget: MDN-MTP: milliseconds per well. GAN+FNN+EnKF with 250 members: seconds to minutes per assimilation step on CPU/GPU (fits a rig budget; likely fits Kaggle budget for offline use) [uncertain].
repeated_layers: Route 2 is the only DL approach here that targets ambiguity directly. MTP/WTA heads keep separate hypotheses for alternative alignments instead of blending them, which addresses exactly our 'blend' failure (15%) and makes 'wrong_mode' (24%) visible as a scored alternative. The 2025 geology-informed correlator adds ordering constraints against repeated-formation errors. Route 1 relies on EM depth-of-investigation to see layers ahead, which GR-only laterals lack.
drift: Not specifically addressed. Route 1's ensemble update can absorb slow structural trends via the latent, but no drift metric is reported.
uncertainty_and_calibration: Both routes output uncertainty (ensemble or K weighted hypotheses). No reliability diagrams, ECE or temperature/isotonic calibration of hypothesis probabilities is reported. EnKF ensembles are known to under-disperse with small ensembles.
where_to_use: (a) A multi-hypothesis (MTP/WTA) auxiliary head on the ConvNeXt/FastViT U-Net decoder: K band-hypothesis TVT curves plus logits per well or per window. Uses: a better-calibrated probability-weighted mean; K-hypothesis features for a reranker/gate; KD targets for the student. (b) A GAN/deep-generative prior for the synthetic well generator, to make structurally realistic hard cases with repeated layers, faults and dip changes. (c) Geology-ordering constraints from DL correlators as a loss term. The EM-based DISTINGUISH workflow itself does not apply, since ROGII has GR only and no UDAR.
error_mode_targeted: Band confusion (~51%: blend 15%, wrong_mode 24%, multimodal_miss 12%) via explicit multi-hypothesis heads; broad/skewed humps (~13%) via mixture components. Not drift.
gap_vs_our_implementation: Our per-column softmax over 400 TVT levels is already a nonparametric multimodal distribution, so a mixture head does not add expressiveness per column. What we lack: (1) hypotheses that are coherent along the whole lateral. The softmax is per column, so modes are not linked into consistent whole-path alternatives, while MTP outputs K complete curves, each internally consistent, with one probability each. That is a path-level mixture, which our failed post-hoc fb continuity decode tried to recover after the fact but never trained for. (2) A training signal that rewards covering the true band as a separate hypothesis (WTA) rather than hedging (blend). (3) Per-hypothesis probabilities that could be calibrated as a K-way classification (temperature scaling on K logits is far easier than calibrating 345x400 softmaxes). (4) A structured generative prior for synthetic data: we use a procedural generator (85% synthetic), not a learned one. Already have: multimodal posterior, expectation decode (RMSE-consistent), an oracle best-mode headroom figure (4.27 ft). The AcfNet unimodal target failed, which is consistent with needing MORE modes handled explicitly, not fewer.
proposed_experiment: E1 (MTP head): in experiments/bilzard/seq_NN_models.py, add an auxiliary head on the U-Net bottleneck/decoder that outputs K=3-4 whole-lateral TVT offset curves (345 columns each), each parameterised as the column-wise soft-argmax over its own 400-level softmax (K extra 400-channel logit maps), plus K well-level logits from global pooling. Loss in seq_NN_train.py: the existing per-column CE plus lambda * [min_k RMSE(curve_k, target) + CE(logits, argmin_k)] with annealed WTA (anneal temperature over epochs to avoid dead heads, per annealed MCL NeurIPS 2024). Decode two ways: (a) the existing expectation decode (control), (b) the calibrated K-weighted mean of curves, with temperature fit on training-fold wells only. Also dump K curves and weights as gate features for the failed ConvNeXt/AnchorCNN gate. Control: the identical 60-epoch ConvNeXt run without the head (5.47 ft), 2 seeds each, holdout 155 wells via seq_NN_holdout_eval.py; success means more than 0.39 ft gain, or oracle-of-K RMSE well below 4.27 ft with weighted-mean RMSE improving. E2 (diagnostic, cheap): from existing posterior dumps (seq_NN_posterior_dump.py --save-all), extract the top-2 path-consistent modes by DP and fit a K=2 weight calibrator (logistic on mode mass, entropy, GR-match score) to measure how much RMSE a perfectly coherent 2-hypothesis representation could gain before building E1.
implementation_effort: Medium for E1: a new head plus loss plus decode, about 150-250 lines; WTA training needs care (hypothesis collapse, annealing schedule). Low for E2 (post-hoc on saved posteriors). High for a GAN-based synthetic generator (training a generative model of real TVT-vs-MD structure from limited real wells).
gpu_cost: E1: about +10-20% memory/compute over the ConvNeXt-small U-Net for K=4 extra 400-level heads; a 60-epoch run on the RTX 5060 8 GB is roughly the same wall time as the baseline and may need a smaller batch [uncertain]. E2: CPU only. The GAN generator route would take several GPU-days of experimentation.
distillation_compatibility: Compatible. The student can distil both the per-column posteriors and the K hypothesis curves and weights (KL on K-way weights, RMSE on curves). The head adds negligible inference cost to FastViT (22 ms budget).
error_correlation_with_ours: As an auxiliary head on the same backbone, errors will be highly correlated, so gains must come from calibration and coherence, not diversity. As features for a gate/reranker, the K-curve set exposes mode alternatives the current gate never sees, which is useful even when correlated.
risk: (1) Under pooled RMSE with a calibrated posterior, the K-weighted mean approaches the expectation decode, so gains appear only if WTA training yields better-calibrated mode weights or brings in evidence the per-column head misses. (2) WTA/MTP heads are prone to collapse and dead hypotheses in data-limited regimes (only real wells carry true ambiguity; 85% synthetic may not contain realistic repeated-band confusions). (3) Prior failures of the unimodal target, axial attention and RAFT at 60 epochs suggest 60 epochs may be too short to judge new heads; budget 150 epochs for a final check. (4) All literature evidence is synthetic and GR-only or EM-based with no RMSE-in-feet numbers, so there is no external proof of benefit on ROGII-like data. (5) GAN geomodels need EM look-ahead data that ROGII lacks.
notes: Overlap: A09 (Alyaev multi-realization / ESS 2022) covers the MDN-MTP head in more depth, and B04 covers annealed/resilient MCL theory; A06 covers the EnKF side of DISTINGUISH. The 2503.08509 paper is labelled GenAI but uses GAN plus EnKF plus DP, not LLMs. No LLM-based geosteering interpretation paper with quantitative results was found. Searches for supervised CNN/LSTM 'relative position to target' predictors on ROGII-like GR laterals found mostly vertical-well correlators (ASDNet, semantic segmentation 2024, Processes 2025) and patents (Chevron US 11480045, covered in A04). The strongest transferable idea for Erudition is the path-level multi-hypothesis output with WTA training and calibrated hypothesis weights.
